timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Do you see yourself, Frank, as competition to the WIF in Davos?
Well, we are not benchmarking ourselves.
We are concentrating our own development.
Definitely, we've got a better weather.
Our meeting is held in Kush Kais in Portugal,
the seaside resort close to Lisbon.
And our mission is to inspire the future.
We are hosting our Horace's global meeting
pretty soon in 10 days time in early May in Kush Kais.
We have around 600 seals from all around the world,
several head of governments in key ministers
and would like to join the shape the future.
Your coverings in pretty big themes aren't you, Frank?
Sustainable development, modeling sustainable migration,
blockchain closing the gender gap, digital future,
embracing AI.
It comes amid an interesting geopolitical backdrop, doesn't it?
No, the current state of the world is quite gloomy.
And I would say that the world is really getting more and more complex
and ultimately maybe even out of balance and out of order.
We see several crises, definitely the crisis in the Middle East,
the rise of populism in the West,
and the demise of globalization in general,
maybe even the lack of leadership and the crisis of leadership.
I believe that many of our leaders are not playing
according to the rules anymore.
Think about trade, think about protectionism
and the current strikes in Syria.
At our meeting, we would like to bring everybody back and say,
you know, we need a multilateral level.
We have to join hands.
We have to join the inspire of the future.
Do you think Macron can inspire President Trump?
He's in Washington.
We've seen the pictures today, Frank.
Do you think he can inspire President Trump to remain on the multilateral,
rather than the unilateral approach?
I'm quite confident that Macron will have some result at the end of the day
and maybe compromise.
Of course, it can't really change President Trump in a day.
But Macron himself has really a figure of flight.
He's a new leader in Europe.
And if it's not him, I think nobody will be able to have an impact on Trump.
They will definitely talk about the deal in Iran.
They talk about climate change and about trade.
And I believe we will see a compromise at the end.
He was unable, though, to twist Trump's arm on the Paris Accord, though,
was he?
So some posing the question, if he can't twist his arm on the Paris Accord,
how can he twist Trump's arm on Iran and trade,
the two big issues?
I think on trade, we'll see a compromise, definitely.
And it will start with China.
The Chinese already made some concessions.
In China now, it's possible to go for a 100% investment,
no longer for joint ventures, like in the manufacturing sector.
And so the Chinese have lead the new force of globalization, if we're able,
playing according to the rules.
And we have to show the Americans that they have to come back to the club.
And Macron is the best person to do that.
What is your community think about China?
Because with China's reaching out to the world,
we had a story yesterday on how it's snapping up.
Tens and tens of European businesses over the last decade.
Or so I can't remember the exact number.
And there are some worries that China's reach is going too far.
What does your business community say about China's reach out into the world?
Our Horat's vision community is quite convinced that China is a new force of globalization.
The new engine of globalization,
think about the one-bell-one road, the new Silk Road,
and bringing money into a central Asia and into Eastern Europe
like a new Marshall blame.
So you think it's a good thing.
And we have to show enhance with the Chinese and help the Chinese.
There's definitely some risk and maybe some fear that Chinese
will take away technology and snap good assets in Europe.
But likewise, European American companies will be able to do so in China as well.
So I think it's a win-win for everybody.
What does your community think about the European backdrop?
We had a 10-year high growth rate within the Eurozone last year.
It seems to just be coming off the boil,
where certainly over the crisis talk, aren't we?
The European sovereign debt crisis era.
Our business leaders encouraged about the future of Europe
when it comes to further integration and the growth prospects.
I think you know the deprecate and even protectionism in the US is a bit of
blessing in disguise for Europe.
Europe is trying to re-engineer itself and try to rethink its goals,
its vision for the future.
On the business side, countries like Portugal are doing very well.
Spain is doing very well.
I think we will continue in the smooth,
but maybe on the mid and long term, maybe another crisis.
I believe in the future, we see many more crisis happening.
In the past, we had to crisis every 30 years, maybe now every seven years.
Some say it takes a crisis for true reform to happen.
Right. You have to wait for the next crisis for maybe the next batch of
integration in Europe to take place or other necessary reforms.
I think Europe is well-prepared now and of course it's nothing is perfect if you wish.
But I think this time it's not so easy to end a crisis again as we did
you know 10 years ago.
The banking sector is like on the right way and real estate of course,
the main source in Spain and Portugal.
But you know my main concern really is trade and what's happening in Washington,
this year.
The Harass is global, meaning May 5th to May 8th,
inspiring our future.
What excites you most, Frank, about this year's gathering?
I think the optimism we feel, you mentioned before, sessions on technology,
on AI, on Internet of Things.
We see a lot of entrepreneurs coming from all around the world talking about the impact
of technology and how we can use technology to reduce poverty.
We got also a lot of African business leaders, we got two African head of states
joining and Africa really is the content end of hope.
And maybe the new China happening now in Africa.
And we want to make this happen, we want to join the shape of the future.

youtube_description: Frank-Jürgen Richter, chairman at Horasis, previews the upcoming Horasis Global Meeting that will bring together 600 CEOs and discusses French President Emmanuel Macron's visit with U.S. President Donald Trump, and the future of trade. He speaks with Bloomberg's Mark Barton on "Bloomberg Markets." (Source: Bloomberg, 25.04.2018)
